insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's protocol converts physical and digital receipts into cryptographically verified purchase events — deterministic proof of transaction rather than behavioral inference. At ~$0.10 per verified receipt, the cost to confirm a real purchase is a fraction of the $5+ CPM brands pay for probabilistic signals that only estimate purchase intent.

Grocery-supermarkets leads all categories at 1,369 receipts and $58,590 GMV in the trailing 14-day window, with Walmart (327), Costco (148), Kroger (143), Publix (131), and Safeway (129) comprising the top five by receipt count. Brands competing in CPG and household goods have the densest verified purchase signal available in this dataset today.

insights.topic: Restaurants & Dining confirmed as a durable category
insights.insight: Restaurants & Dining first appeared October 30 and has held 1,004–1,028 receipts across multiple rolloff cycles before settling at 1,014 in the November 1 snapshot — persistence through two distinct rolloff events suggests organic signal, not a data artifact. QSR and casual dining brands now have a confirmed category footprint to evaluate.

insights.topic: Gas & convenience channel expanding with named brands
insights.insight: 7-Eleven crossed the brand visibility threshold October 30 and Circle K followed October 31, joining a gas-convenience category that already carries 617 receipts and $24,533 GMV in the 14-day window. Two brand additions in under 48 hours broke a 40-snapshot freeze — the channel is actively onboarding, not static.

insights.topic: Digital receipt verification covers AI and e-commerce platforms
insights.insight: The confirmed DKIM vendor list includes Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Suno — spanning e-commerce transactions, subscription payments, and AI service purchases. Brands targeting digitally active, subscription-paying consumers have a verified purchase signal path that does not depend on cookie-based tracking.

insights.topic: Settlement cadence is episodic, not continuous
insights.insight: 809 confirmed payouts have produced no new settlements across 35+ consecutive snapshots spanning a full calendar week — burst windows separated by extended zero-payout periods are the established pattern. Brands evaluating this as a real-time activation channel should model latency into any campaign timing assumption.
